messages:
Evan Brooks: Hey team, day 3 q: where do I post different onboarding problems (VPN, laptop shipping, repo access)? Also: which bots are ok to poke in channels and which should I only DM?
Kiran Patel: Welcome Evan! Short map: laptop & HR logistics -> #people-ops (use the pinned form). VPN and infra access -> #eng-infra. Repo/org invites -> open SSO access via the link in #help and include your GitHub handle.
Lina Ortiz: If it's blocking you (no VPN, can't clone), post in #help and mention @eng-oncall. That channel is monitored during business hours.
Evan Brooks: Sweet. I saw a "fun-polls" bot in #random and a deploy app in #eng-releases  safe to try?
Kiran Patel: Rule of thumb: sandbox/test-labeled bots are fine in public. For anything deploy/infra-related, use #dev-playground or DM the bot. Dont run unknown slash commands in org-wide channels.
Devex Bot: Tip: to test integrations use #dev-playground. Run commands there or DM me to avoid noisy posts. Use `/devex help` for a list of safe sandbox commands.
Evan Brooks: Nice. Any quick etiquette bullets so I don't clog channels?
Lina Ortiz: TL;DR: 1) Search Slack + handbook first. 2) Pick the most specific channel (avoid #general). 3) Use threads for follow-ups. 4) Paste short logs in fenced code blocks (5-10 lines). 5) For long traces use an unlisted gist. 6) Never paste secrets in Slack.
Evan Brooks: If I accidentally paste a secret, what's the flow?
Kiran Patel: Delete the message, rotate the credential immediately, then ping #eng-security. They have a pinned runbook for secrets rotation.
HR Bot: For hardware or shipping changes open https://peopleops.internal/tickets and include your manager and shipping address. Mark the ticket "urgent" if its blocking you.
Evan Brooks: Awesome, that clears things up. I'll use #help for blocking issues and #dev-playground for bot tests. Thanks everyone! :raised_hands:
